scope: Read-only 40B record streaming; timestamps are host kernel arrival and passive user receive, not physical transmitter timing.
caveats: Local SocketCAN companion receives other local sockets' transmitted frames through software loopback; its command frames do not establish bus ACK, delivery to motor, or physical movement.
No tx_errors/tx_dropped counter increase does not negate the SDK SEND_MESSAGE_FAILED exception; the failed enqueue/send may not reach netdevice transmit accounting.
schedstat samples are about one second apart and do not identify which Python thread was in which SDK call; they cannot by themselves prove the send failure was caused by scheduling.
SO_RXQ_OVFL cumulative observer counter cannot measure upstream USB/CAN driver loss or losses in the separate Piper socket.

final_command_group_incomplete.interpretation: Last observed group has 151/155/156 without a later 157, consistent with an interrupted send sequence. This cannot alone prove which call failed or why.

findings.interface_counters: rx_dropped stayed at historical 75826; rx_errors, tx_errors and tx_dropped stayed at zero. tx_packets reached 24503 by 16:15:28.283 and remained 24503 at 16:15:33.696.
findings.passive_observer: Cumulative SO_RXQ_OVFL is zero. Largest kernel-to-user reader lag inside the ten-second window is 172.427397ms; that is observer scheduling/backlog, not CAN wire latency.
findings.piper_sampling: Piper main process snapshots are S/R, 19 threads, about 510-570ms aggregate CPU per roughly 1.1s sample. Main and TID53751 show runnable queue wait both before and after the send error; no unique exception-time process freeze is established.
findings.memory: Available memory in the bracketing samples remains about 1.82-1.86GiB. These samples do not support memory exhaustion as this exception's established cause.
findings.root_cause_limit: Driver log proves SEND_MESSAGE_FAILED then latched stop. Current record cannot distinguish SDK/socket enqueue failure, host scheduling/transport details or bus/controller causes; no generic hardware-fault conclusion.
